shots.title: Define human, agent, and internal command audiences with promotion/demotion rules
shots.notes: Classified every top-level command registry entry into human, agent, advanced, or internal audiences and wrote promotion/demotion rules for the future surface model.

shots.title: Design the small human command cockpit and default help surface
shots.notes: Defined the proposed human cockpit around now, start, briefing, review, doctor, card, and help --all, with output budgets and backing primitives.

shots.title: Design skill-first agent workflows that hide CLI plumbing behind outcome commands
shots.notes: Mapped common human asks to skill-first workflows and identified the hidden CLI/MCP primitives each skill may orchestrate without teaching the whole command list to humans.

shots.title: Design bounded roadmap planning views as one case study of the new surface model
shots.notes: Specified a bounded roadmap status contract and added S149-S151 as the implementation runway. Raised #539 for the S147 shipped-reference false positive instead of hiding it in this planning sprint.

conditions.description: The planning sprint exposed that roadmap validation can mistake issue-fix keys such as S147-533 for shipped roadmap sprint evidence.
Current roadmap status output prints almost the entire historical roadmap and critical path, which made the product-surface problem concrete.

training.description: A human-facing SLOPE command must be bounded, decision-oriented, and safe to run without prior protocol context.
training.outcome: S148 defines audience rules and a seven-entry cockpit to keep the remembered surface small.

training.description: Roadmap verbosity is a symptom of a broader audience-boundary issue, not the whole problem.
training.outcome: S148 keeps roadmap status as a case study while routing implementation into S149-S151.

nutrition.description: Created docs/backlog/sprint-148-human-surface-simplification.md with taxonomy, cockpit, skill workflow contract, roadmap case study, and implementation backlog.
Updated docs/backlog/roadmap.json with S149-S151 as the Phase 47 implementation lane.
Roadmap JSON parsing passed and roadmap validation showed only the known S147/#539 error before S148 closeout status was applied.
Scorecard validation, map --check, git diff --check, and GitHub CI should remain the closeout gates for this planning PR.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: Clarifying. The command list is not bad because it is large; it is bad because humans and agents are being asked to stand in the same doorway.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Fix the roadmap signal first, then make audience metadata enforceable in the registry before adding new cockpit aliases.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The roadmap status command produced the exact failure mode the sprint was trying to name: too much true information, too little decision shape.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: SLOPE can keep its rich execution machinery while giving humans a much calmer surface.

bunker_locations: Roadmap validation should not treat issue-fix keys like S147-533 as shipped evidence for roadmap sprint S147.
Human-facing commands need explicit output budgets or they drift toward full internal state dumps.
yardage_book_updates: docs/backlog/sprint-148-human-surface-simplification.md defines the audience taxonomy, proposed cockpit, skill-first workflow contract, roadmap default-output spec, and S149-S151 implementation backlog.
docs/backlog/roadmap.json now extends Phase 47 through S151 and makes S149 responsible for #539 plus bounded roadmap status.
course_management_notes: GitHub issue #539 was opened for the S147 shipped-reference false positive.
Draft PR #540 carries the S148 planning lane.
S147 remains a separate planned handoff-continuity sprint rather than a blocker for the human-surface lane.
